content: 1. A study conducted in South Africa evaluated the use of chemotherapy in therapy-naïve patients with HIV-associated Kaposi sarcoma. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012, volume 60, issue 2, pages 150–157. 2. Bagatell FK conducted a prospective study on the efficacy of bifonazole 1% cream applied once daily for the treatment of tinea corporis and tinea cruris. This research was published in Advances in Therapy in 1986, volume 3, issue 5, pages 294–300. 3. Dobson RL, Bagatell FK, Hickman JG, Whitmore CG, Willis I, Seffon J, and colleagues investigated the use of naftifine 1% cream in treating tinea cruris and tinea corporis. Their findings appeared in Drug Investigation in 1991, volume 3, issue 1, pages 57–59. 4. Hantschke D and Reichenberger M conducted a double-blind, randomized, comparative in vivo study to evaluate the antifungal efficacy of clotrimazole, tolnaftate, and naftifine. This study was published in Mykosen in 1980, volume 23, issue 12, pages 657–668 (in German). 5. Haroon TS, Hussain I, Aman S, and Jahangir M performed a randomized, comparative study of naftifine 1% cream (applied once daily) versus tioconazole 1% cream (applied twice daily) for the treatment of tinea cruris. The results were published in the Pakistan Journal of Medical Sciences Quarterly in 1996, volume 12, issue 2, pages 181–184. 6. Jerajani HR, Janaki C, Kumar S, and Phiske M conducted a pilot study comparing the efficacy and safety of sertaconazole 2% cream, terbinafine 1% cream, and luliconazole 1% cream in patients with dermatophytoses. This study was published in the Indian Journal of Dermatology in 2013, volume 58, issue 1, pages 34–38. 7. Katz HI, Bard J, Cole GW, Fischer S, McCormick GE, Medansky RS, and colleagues evaluated the use of SCH 370 (a combination of clotrimazole and betamethasone dipropionate) cream in patients with tinea cruris or tinea corporis. Their findings were published in Cutis in 1984, volume 34, issue 2, pages 183–188. 8. Lebwohl M, Elewski B, Eisen D, and Savin RC assessed the efficacy and safety of terbinafine 1% solution in treating interdigital tinea pedis, tinea corporis, and tinea cruris. This study was published in Cutis in 2001, volume 67, issue 3, pages 261–266. 9. Li M, Bi ZG, Gu J, Sheng YN, Zhang MH, Wang Y, and colleagues conducted a clinical study on butenafine hydrochloride 1% cream for the treatment of tinea pedis, tinea corporis, and tinea cruris. The results were published in the Journal of Clinical Dermatology in 2006, volume 35, issue 7, pages 471–472. 10. Millikan LE evaluated the efficacy and tolerability of topical terbinafine in treating tinea cruris. The findings were published in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology, volume 2, pages 795–799. 11. Miura Y, Onuki M, Takahashi S, Seiji M, Sato A, Kagawa S, and colleagues conducted a double-blind study on the utility of econazole cream in dermatomycosis. This study was published in Rinsho Hyoka (Clinical Evaluation) in 1979, volume 7, issue 1, pages 83–108. 12. Pariser RJ and Pariser DM compared the clinical and mycological effects of clotrimazole/betamethasone dipropionate cream versus ketoconazole cream in patients with tinea cruris. Their findings were published in the Journal of Dermatological Treatment in 1995, volume 6, issue 3, pages 173–177. 13. Ramam M, Prasas HR, Manchanda Y, Khaitan BK, Banerjee U, Mukhopadhyaya A, and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial on topical butenafine for tinea cruris and tinea corporis. The results were published in the Indian Journal of Dermatology, Venereology, and Leprology in 2003, volume 69, issue 2, pages 154–158. 14. Shen WM, Hu YW, and Gu HY compared econazole compound cream with miconazole cream in treating tinea corporis and tinea cruris. This study was published in the Chinese Journal of New Drugs and Clinical Remedies in 2002, volume 21, issue 3, pages 143–145. 15. Singal A, Pandhi D, Agrawal S, and Das S conducted a randomized, double-blind trial comparing the efficacy of topical 1% butenafine and 1% clotrimazole in tinea cruris and tinea corporis. The findings were published in the Journal of Dermatological Treatment in 2005, volume 16, issues 5–6, pages 331–335. 16. Spiekermann PH and Young MD evaluated the clinical efficacy of clotrimazole, a broad-spectrum antifungal agent. This study was published in the Archives of Dermatology in 1976, volume 112, issue 3, pages 350–352. 17. Tanenbaum L, Taplin D, Lavelle C, Akers WA, Rosenberg MJ, and Carmargo G assessed the use of sulconazole nitrate 1% cream for treating tinea cruris and tinea corporis. Their findings were published in Cutis in 1989, volume 44, issue 4, pages 344–347. 18. Wang AP, Li RY, Shun QN, Wan Z, Wang XH, Wang JB, and colleagues conducted a double-blind, randomized controlled clinical trial on econazole-triamcinolone acetonide cream for tinea pedis, tinea corporis, and tinea cruris. The results were published in the Chinese Journal of Clinical Pharmacology in 2000, volume 16, issue 5, pages 345–349. 19. Wortzel MH conducted a double-blind study comparing the superiority of a combination antifungal (clotrimazole) and steroidal (betamethasone dipropionate) product. This study was published in Cutis in 1982, volume 30, issue 2, pages 258–261. 20. Zaias N, Berman B, Cordero CN, Hernandez A, Jacobson C, Millikan L, and colleagues evaluated the efficacy of a 1-week, once-daily regimen of terbinafine 1% cream for tinea cruris and tinea corporis. The findings were published in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology in 1993, volume 29, issue 4, pages 646–648. 21. De Wit D, O’Doherty E, De Vroey C, and Clumeck N compared the safety and efficacy of single-dose fluconazole with a 7-day regimen of itraconazole for AIDS-related oropharyngeal candidiasis. This study was published in the Journal of International Medical Research in 1998, volume 26, issue 3, pages 159–170. 22. Linpiyawan R, Jittreprasert K, and Sivayathorn A conducted a clinical trial comparing clotrimazole troche with itraconazole oral solution for oral candidosis in AIDS patients. The findings were published in the International Journal of Dermatology in 2000, volume 39, issue 11, pages 859–861.
